lots.guide_summary: 6 sold, 0 unsold, 1 asking. Five recent European and US sales of labelled genuine PH5s ran AUD 389 to 714, all at or below estimate for the design houses, and one older Leonard Joel sale was AUD 744. The one dealer asking price is AUD 991, above the sold range. Rates: EUR 1 = AUD 1.6211 and USD 1 = AUD 1.4276 (ECB 29 Sep 2026). All of this assumes lot 87 is a genuine Louis Poulsen example. If it is a copy, it is worth perhaps AUD 50 to 150.
lots.working: These figures apply only if a Louis Poulsen label or stamp is confirmed. Keep: lowest surviving SOLD AUD 389 (Dannenberg EUR 240) / 1.22 = 318.9, rounded down to 315 (all-in 315 x 1.22 = 384.30). Flip: likely resale AUD 550 (between the European sales at AUD 389-454, the Wright sale at AUD 714 and the Leonard Joel sale at AUD 744), less 15% selling fees (AUD 82.50) and AUD 30 for packing or outbound postage = AUD 437.50, / 2.44 = 179.3, rounded down to 175 (all-in 213.50). If it is unlabelled or a copy, treat both as 0.
lots.confidence_reason: There is no maker's label or mark in the photos. The form, the blue ring and the violet struts are right for a genuine PH5, but copies exist. The SOLD evidence is good (five recent results) and is all for labelled genuine lamps. The prices come from the embedded data of the Invaluable artist page, not the displayed page, and it is not stated whether they are hammer or include premium.

lots.question_for_armitage: Is there a Louis Poulsen label or stamp inside the top shade or on the socket housing? Are the shades free of dents, and is the small red lower cone present? Please also note the wiring is old and will need replacing.
